'''Ronald Shavlik Randolph''' (born November 24, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]] after a decorated high school career. After going undrafted in the [[2005 NBA draft]], Randolph played parts of eight seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).

In addition to playing in the NBA, Randolph has played in China and Puerto Rico, averaging a league-high 32.0 points per game during the [[2012–13 CBA season]] and was ranked in the top-five for rebounds per game in both his seasons in the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>[http://www.bsnpr.com/jugadores/jugador.asp?id=2692 ESTADÍSTICAS JUGADOR – Randolph, Shavlik]</ref>

==High school career==
Randolph attended [[Needham B. Broughton High School|Broughton High School]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]]. He scored 56 points in a game to surpass Broughton High alum [[Pete Maravich]]'s all-time single-game record and later, passed him in career points, rebounds and blocks as well.<ref>[https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1572669-meet-shavlik-randolph-possible-x-factor-for-a-boston-celtics-playoff-drive Meet Shavlik Randolph, Possible Missing Link for a Boston Celtics Playoff Drive]</ref>

Randolph was a [[McDonald's All-American]], two-time Parade All-American, and a two-time [[Associated Press]] North Carolina Player of the Year. As a junior in 2000–01, he averaged 27.9 points and 13.2 rebounds per game. As a senior in 2001–02, he averaged 30 points, 14 rebounds and five blocks per game.<ref name=bio>[http://www.nba.com/media/sixers/ShavlickRandolph.pdf SHAVLIK RANDOLPH – Philadelphia 76ers media guide]</ref>

As a senior, Randolph was rated as the #6 power forward in the nation by [[Scout.com]].<ref>{{cite web|title=SCOUT.COM COLLEGE BASKETBALL TEAM RECRUITING PROSPECTS – 2002 POWER FORWARD|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=44&yr=2002|work=Scout.com|access-date=October 29, 2014}}</ref>

==College career==
Randolph started his college career with [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] by scoring a team-high 23 points and adding 7 rebounds in his November 23, 2002, debut against [[Army Black Knights men's basketball|Army]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=223270150 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20021209102356/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=223270150 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 9, 2002 |title=Randolph's gift to Duke - 23 on opening night |work=ESPN.com |date=November 23, 2002 |access-date=May 2, 2013}}</ref> Two days later, Randolph posted his first double-double against [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=223290150 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130103023004/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=223290150 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 3, 2013 |title=Duhon leads the show for the Blue Devils |work=ESPN.com |date=November 25, 2002 |access-date=May 2, 2013}}</ref> Randolph's performance, however, started to decline after this stellar start, only scoring in double figures in five other games for the rest of the season. He suffered from numerous injuries which limited his playing time. He played in twenty-six games his freshman year (with six starts), averaging 7.4 points and 3.9 rebounds per game.<ref name=stats>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/shavlik-randolph-1.html |title=Shavlik Randolph Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=October 29, 2014}}</ref>

In May 2003, Randolph had successful surgery on his left hip to correct a labral tear and bone spur.<ref name="bio" /> In his sophomore year, Randolph played in all 37 of Duke's games, averaging 7.0 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.6 blocks per game.<ref name="stats" /> Randolph's game excelled during Duke's 2004 run to the [[Final Four]]. In the opening round, Randolph posted 20 points, 8 rebounds and 2 steals against [[Alabama State University|Alabama State]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=244000016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040917225328/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=244000016 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 17, 2004 |title=Randolph's 20 aids Blue Devil rout |work=ESPN.com |date=March 18, 2004 |access-date=May 2, 2013}}</ref> Randolph also played well in the national semi-final game against [[Connecticut Huskies|UConn]], scoring 13 points on 6-for-6 shooting with six rebounds and one blocked shot.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=244000062 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040505145901/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=244000062 |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 5, 2004 |title=Okafor: All 18 points after halftime |work=ESPN.com |date=April 3, 2004 |access-date=May 2, 2013}}</ref>

In his junior year, Randolph averaged 4.4 points and 4.3 rebounds in 29 games (18.9 mpg). He sat out four games during the season after being diagnosed with [[Infectious mononucleosis|mononucleosis]], and slowly worked his way back into the rotation. He eventually returned to his starting role, giving the Blue Devils another inside presence to go with center [[Shelden Williams]].<ref name="bio" />

On May 13, 2005, Randolph declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final year of college eligibility.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=149768 |title=Duke's Shavlik Randolph Declares Himself Eligible For The NBA Draft |access-date=October 29, 2014 |archive-date=October 29, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029110646/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=149768 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In his three-year career at Duke, he played 92 games (36 starts) while averaging 6.3 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.4 blocks per game. He was also a member of two ACC regular season championships, two ACC tournament championships, and one Final Four appearance.

==Professional career==
===Philadelphia 76ers (2005–2008)===
Randolph went undrafted in the [[2005 NBA draft]]. On August 5, 2005, he signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/gai-randolph-sixers-080505.shtml 76ers sign Randolph, Gai]</ref> On June 30, 2006, the 76ers tendered a qualifying offer to make Randolph a restricted free agent.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20141111184933/http://articles.philly.com/2006-07-02/sports/25405042_1_salary-cap-sixers-green-and-randolph Sixers keen on Pistons' Ben Wallace Billy King contacted the player's agent, hoping to fill a big void with strong defense and rebounding]</ref>

On July 12, 2006, Randolph re-signed with the 76ers to a two-year, $2.1 million contract with the second year containing a player option.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=397500 |title=Shavlik Randolph Re-signs With Sixers |access-date=October 29, 2014 |archive-date=October 29, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029110643/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=397500 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=2517179 76ers re-sign forward Randolph]</ref> Two days later, he joined the 76ers for the 2006 [[Rocky Mountain Revue]].<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Philadelphia-Sixers/22/Rosters/Summer_League/2006 2006-2007 Philadelphia Sixers Summer League Rosters]</ref>

On November 30, 2006, Randolph broke his left ankle at practice and was taken by ambulance to a hospital. He was playing defense when he landed on the foot of [[Andre Iguodala]].<ref>[http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/sixers/2006-11-30-randolph_x.htm Sixers forward Shavlik Randolph breaks ankle at practice]</ref> He was subsequently ruled out for the rest of the 2006–07 season.

On June 22, 2007, Randolph exercised the player option on his contract, keeping him with the team for a third season.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=tx76ersrandolph 76ers F Randolph picks up player option on contract]</ref> In July 2007, he re-joined the 76ers for the 2007 NBA Summer League but did not end up playing for them in either the Las Vegas entry or the Rocky Mountain Revue entry.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/summerleague2007/team/index.jsp?team=sixers 2007 76ers Summer League Team] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150119225252/http://www.nba.com/summerleague2007/team/index.jsp?team=sixers |date=January 19, 2015 }}</ref><ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Philadelphia-Sixers/22/Rosters/Summer_League/2007 2007-2008 Philadelphia Sixers Summer League Rosters]</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers and Miami Heat (2008–2010)===
[[File:Shavlik Randolph signs basketball for young fan.jpg|thumb|Shavlik Randolph signs a basketball for a young fan at [[Eglin Air Force Base]] in 2010]]
On September 25, 2008, Randolph signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=1760 Trail Blazers sign Shavlik Randolph]</ref> His first game of the 2008–09 season came on January 14, 2009, against his former team, the 76ers, where he managed four points in as many minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290114020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090125072755/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290114020 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 25, 2009 |title=Iguodala notches season-high 29 to lead Sixers' romp over Blazers |work=ESPN.com |date=January 14, 2009 |access-date=May 2, 2013}}</ref>

On September 28, 2009, Randolph signed with the [[Miami Heat]]. He managed just two games for the Heat before he was waived on December 14, 2009.<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=5143 Heat waive Shavlik Randolph]</ref> On December 30, 2009, he re-signed with the Trail Blazers to help the team deal with numerous injuries. Portland had to use an NBA hardship exemption in order to sign him as he made their roster stand at 16, one over the allowed limited of 15.<ref>[http://www.columbian.com/news/2009/dec/30/blazers-sign-randolph/ Blazers sign Randolph, who re-joins his old team]</ref> His second stint did not last long as he was waived by Portland on January 6 after playing just three games.<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=5236 Trail Blazers waive Shavlik Randolph]</ref> However, two days later, he signed a 10-day contract with the Trail Blazers.<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=5244 Trail Blazers sign Shavlik Randolph to 10-day contract]</ref> After his 10-day contract expired, he parted ways with the team.

On April 6, 2010, Randolph re-signed with the Heat for the rest of the 2009–10 season.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_sign_shavlik_randolph_2010.html HEAT Sign Shavlik Randolph]</ref> In early July 2010, he joined the Heat for the 2010 NBA Summer League where he averaged 13.0 points and 5.8 rebounds in four games.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/summerleague2010/teams/heat/ 2010 Heat Summer League Team]</ref> On July 27, 2010, he again re-signed with the Heat<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5414436 Forward Randolph rejoins Heat]</ref> but was later waived on October 20, 2010, before the start of the 2010–11 season.<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=6693 Heat waive Kenny Hasbrouck and Shavlik Randolph]</ref>

===Puerto Rico and China (2011–2012)===
In March 2011, Randolph signed with [[Gallitos de Isabela]] for the 2011 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] season.<ref>[http://www.blazersedge.com/2011/3/31/2083679/shavlik-randolph-signs-with-gallitos-de-isabela-in-puerto-rico Shavlik Randolph Signs With Gallitos de Isabela In Puerto Rico]{{Dead link|date=March 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

In October 2011, Randolph signed with the [[Dongguan Leopards]] for the [[2011–12 CBA season]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.blazersedge.com/2011/10/3/2466180/former-blazers-f-shavlik-randolph-signs-with-dongguan-in-china |title=Former Blazers F Shavlik Randolph Signs With Dongguan In China |access-date=October 29, 2014 |archive-date=October 29, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029111009/http://www.blazersedge.com/2011/10/3/2466180/former-blazers-f-shavlik-randolph-signs-with-dongguan-in-china |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On April 9, 2012, Randolph signed with [[Piratas de Quebradillas]] for the 2012 BSN season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/91308/piratas-de-quebradillas-announce-shavlik-randolph.html Piratas de Quebradillas announce Shavlik Randolph]</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2012)===
In July 2012, Randolph joined the [[Washington Wizards]] for the 2012 NBA Summer League.<ref>[http://www.bulletsforever.com/2012/7/12/3155210/nba-summer-league-2012-schedule-wizards-roster Washington Wizards Summer League Roster, Schedule, TV Information And More]</ref> On September 19, 2012, he signed with the Wizards.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-four-training-camp |title=Wizards Sign Four For Training Camp |work=NBA.com |date=September 19, 2012 |access-date=May 2, 2013}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Wizards on October 27, 2012, before the start of the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11316 |title=Wizards waive Shavlik Randolph and Steven Gray |work=InsideHoops.com |date=October 27, 2012 |access-date=May 2, 2013}}</ref>

===Foshan Long Lions (2012–2013)===
On November 23, 2012, Randolph signed with the [[Foshan Long Lions]] for the rest of the [[2012–13 CBA season]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/96804/shavlik-randolph-signs-in-china-with-foshan.html Shavlik Randolph signs in China with Foshan]</ref> On February 5, 2013, he signed with [[Cangrejeros de Santurce (basketball)|Cangrejeros de Santurce]] for the 2013 BSN season.<ref>[http://www.indicepr.com/noticias/2013/02/06/sports/959/randolph-a-los-cangrejeros/ Randolph a los Cangrejeros] {{in lang|es}}</ref> However, following the CBA season, he returned to the United States with hopes of re-joining the NBA.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/99611/shavlik-randolph-plans-to-sign-in-the-nba.html Shavlik Randolph plans to sign in the NBA]</ref> In 28 games for Foshan, he averaged 32.0 points, 14.6 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.7 steals per game.

===Boston Celtics (2013)===
On March 1, 2013, Randolph signed a 10-day contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-sign-shavlik-randolph |title=Celtics Sign Shavlik Randolph |work=NBA.com |date=March 1, 2013 |access-date=May 2, 2013}}</ref> On March 11, 2013, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-sign-randolph-second-10-day |title=Celtics Sign Randolph to Second 10-Day |work=NBA.com |date=March 11, 2013 |access-date=May 2, 2013}}</ref> On March 21, 2013, he signed a multi-year contract with the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-sign-randolph-multi-year-contract |title=Celtics Sign Randolph to Multi-Year Contract |work=NBA.com |date=March 21, 2013 |access-date=May 2, 2013}}</ref> On August 1, 2013, he was waived by the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-waive-randolph|title=Celtics Waive Randolph|work=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2013|access-date=August 1, 2013}}</ref>

===Return to Foshan (2013)===
In October 2013, Randolph re-signed with the Foshan Long Lions for the [[2013–14 CBA season]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/106579/shavlik-randolph-will-play-again-in-china.html Shavlik Randolph will play again in China]</ref><ref>[http://cbachina.sports.sohu.com/20131003/n387594276.shtml 白兰多夫正式与佛山续约 重返CBA年薪至少150万] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004225104/http://cbachina.sports.sohu.com/20131003/n387594276.shtml |date=October 4, 2013 }} {{in lang|zh}}</ref> However, just six games into the season, he was ruled out for 4–5 weeks with a left shoulder injury and was replaced in the line-up by [[Dexter Pittman]] on December 3, 2013.<ref>[http://www.asiancagers.com/nba-center-dexter-pittman-will-replace-injured-shavlik-randolph-in-foshan/ CBA: NBA Center Dexter Pittman will Replace Injured Shavlik Randolph in Foshan] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029115448/http://www.asiancagers.com/nba-center-dexter-pittman-will-replace-injured-shavlik-randolph-in-foshan/ |date=October 29, 2014 }}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2014–2015)===
On March 1, 2014, Randolph signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]] for the rest of the 2013–14 season, with a team option for 2014–15.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-randolph-waive-kravtsov Suns Sign Randolph, Waive Kravtsov]</ref><ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/232208/Shavlik-Randolph-Signs-With-Suns-For-Remainder-Of-Season Shavlik Randolph Signs With Suns For Remainder Of Season]</ref> He made his debut off the bench a day later against the [[Atlanta Hawks]], recording 2 points, 2 rebounds and 1 steal in the 129–120 win.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20140302/ATLPHX/gameinfo.html Notebook: Suns 129, Hawks 120]</ref> His contract became fully guaranteed for 2014–15 after the Suns did not release him prior to the July 17 cut off date.<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234345/Suns-To-Keep-Shavlik-Randolph-Beyond-Contract-Guarantee-Date-For-14-15 Suns To Keep Shavlik Randolph Beyond Contract Guarantee Date For 14-15]</ref>

===Return to Boston (2015)===
On January 15, 2015, Randolph was acquired by the [[Boston Celtics]] in a three-team trade also involving the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-complete-three-team-trade-20150115 Boston Celtics Complete Three-Team Trade]</ref> On April 6, 2015, he was waived by the Celtics after appearing in just five games.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-sign-babb Boston Celtics Sign Babb]</ref>

On April 8, 2015, Randolph was claimed off waivers by the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/237360/Shavlik-Randolph-Claimed-By-Nuggets-Off-Waivers Shavlik Randolph Claimed By Nuggets Off Waivers]</ref> However, he was later released by the Nuggets before appearing in a game for them.<ref>[http://www.denverpost.com/nuggets/ci_27881431/nuggets-expected-release-shavlik-randolph-salary-cap-move Nuggets expected to release Shavlik Randolph in salary-cap move for future]</ref>

===Return to China (2015–2019)===
On July 31, 2015, Randolph signed a three-year deal with the [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/171110/liaoning-flying-leopards-sign-shavlik-randolph.html Liaoning Flying Leopards sign Shavlik Randolph]</ref><ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/172595/shavlik-randolph-will-get-at-least-dollars7m-in-china-in-three-years.html Shavlik Randolph will get at least $7M in China in three years]</ref>

==Off the court==
Randolph is a co-founder of North Carolina–based Big Prime Hauling, which was acquired by Bright Hope Capital in August 2020. He is also credited, along with several other NBA players, as an early investor in Fotmer Life Sciences, LLC., founded in South America in 2016.

==Personal life==
Randolph is the son of Ken and Kim Randolph who both attended the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]]. His grandfather, [[Ronnie Shavlik]], was an [[All-America]]n basketball player at [[North Carolina State University|N.C. State]] and a first-round draft pick of the New York Knicks in [[1956 NBA draft|1956]]. As a child, Randolph worked as a ball boy for the N.C. State team.<ref>[http://www.complex.com/sports/2013/03/the-20-most-hated-duke-players-of-all-time/shavlik-randolph The 20 Most-Hated Duke Players of All Time]</ref> He also has a brother, Dexter and a sister, Senna.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/media/48295_02_PLAYERS_25-104.pdf |title=PLAYERS – Miami Heat media guide |access-date=May 2, 2013}}</ref> His brother Dexter, died on October 8, 2019, in [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], Japan.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.dignitymemorial.com/obituaries/raleigh-nc/dexter-randolph-8886240|title=Dexter Randolph Obituary}}</ref>
